Records the approval. No credential is created here. Keys are
self-serve, so an approval no longer gates them; it is linked to the
requester's next key for its history.

Repeating the same decision returns 200 without re-emitting the
notification; the opposite decision on an already-decided request
returns 409.

operations.description:
Opens a request for programmatic access. API keys no longer need an
approval (`POST /me/api-keys` is self-serve), so this is optional: it
tells the foundation about an integration. An approved request that has
not produced a key yet is linked to the next key the requester creates.

Only one request may be open at a time; asking again while one is pending
returns 409.

Creates a new API key for the current user and returns the full secret
exactly once. The key authenticates as the owning user when sent as
`Authorization: Bearer <key>`, both on this API and on the grower MCP
server.

Keys are self-serve: no approved access request is needed. Each key is
metered on the integration usage plan, and a user may hold at most five
live keys; creating a sixth returns 409 until one is revoked. An
approved access request that has not produced a key yet is linked to
the new key for its history.
